facts.text: Sizzling over the fire in Fagin's den the night Oliver arrives
facts.why: Fagin tells the Dodger to take off the sausages and lay a place for Mr Twist when Oliver reaches the den, and the sausages are mouldy.

facts.text: The first proper breakfast in the big house in Bloomsbury
facts.why: The transcript has Mr Brownlow and Mrs Bedwin caring for Oliver but no breakfast scene, and Bloomsbury is never named.
facts.fix: A proper breakfast for Oliver, safe in Mr Brownlow's house

facts.text: Saffron Hill, London. Up the stairs, mind the rats.
facts.why: The film never names Saffron Hill. That is Dickens' address from the novel, and the film only shows Fagin's den in London.
facts.fix: Fagin's den, London. Up the stairs, mind the rats.

vibe.verdict: A good newspaper concept with the right dishes and winks, though the look is flat and the masthead price is American.
missing: 'Please sir, I want some more' (workhouse dining hall)
Consider Yourself with the Dodger (London streets)
The bookstall wallet theft with Mr Brownlow (London)
Nancy and the Three Cripples sing-along (tavern)
Fagin's treasure sinking in the mud (finale)
ideas: Change 'Two cents' on the masthead to 'Tuppence'.
Swap 'Workhouse porridge brulee' for a plain 'Please sir, one more bowl' gruel with a burnt sugar top.
Swap the Brownlow crumpets note for the bookstall wallet theft.
Make the second page photo a colour frame so the paper looks less washed out.
